newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan opposition takes two Taleban towns.
newsitem.headline: Afghan opposition takes two Taleban towns.

text.p: Opposition forces on Friday captured two strategic Afghan towns north of the capital Kabul from the Taleban Islamic militia and were fighting for a third, a Pakistan-based Afghan news service said.

The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) quoted its sources as saying in Afghanistan that forces loyal to Ahmad Shah Masood had seized Golbahar, at the mouth of his native Panjsher Valley, and nearby Jabal-os-Siraj in Parwan province, after heavy fighting.
It said Masood's forces were now fighting further south aiming to take Charikar, capital of Parwan province.
AIP said Taleban had sent reinforcements from Kabul to join up with the retreating militia fighters from Jabal-os-Siraj, which lies about 80 km (50 miles) on the main highway north of Kabul.
